nonvacuity: Closed concrete example: the sole outcome of censusDesign has probability 1 and samples both units, with outcomes (0,1). The normalized and physical weights at alpha=beta=1 are (1,1), with positive denominator 2. The two least indices are actually 0 and 1. The retained statements refute the printed proof steps; they do not purport to refute the endpoint results. The omitted singleton box, endpoint/mean identities and explicit formula evaluation are accurately disclosed.

Compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean using only Defs: N=J=2, class map id, outcomes (0,1), and a design returning either the empty sample or the two-unit census, each with probability 1/2. With alpha=1/4 and beta=3/4, all inclusions equal 1/2 and even separation holds (gamma=3, class totals (1/2,1/2)). The chosen discrete measurable structure gives jointLaw total mass 1. Thus the hypotheses allow empty samples, dependence within a sample, distinct classes and strict bounds. The unconditional result also applies to the nonseparated design in T14.

Closed random design on six units with eight equiprobable outcomes, selecting one unit from each of three pairs. Every replicate has one observation of each outcome 0,2,3, so every positive-length pooled sample is nonempty. Independent exact box-vertex arithmetic confirms attained extrema 5/4 and 2. The upper threshold value 2 equals the middle outcome, so failure of separation is real, while the actual pooled extrema are constant on every path. The polynomial certificates, specified optimizer evaluations and pooled onto-box identity are accurately disclosed as omitted.

Compiled two-class compatibility instances in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean: y=(0,1), q=(1/2,1/2), alpha=1/4, beta=1/2, m=(1,1), T=1; and alpha=beta=1/2, q=(1/3,2/3), m=(1,2), T=3/2. All class sizes and masses are positive. Absolute compatibility is equivalent to the existence of bounded per-unit marginal vectors; any such vector is realizable by finite independent Bernoulli sampling. The existence hypothesis is canonical. The richer-information failure assertion and the two automatic-compatibility assertions are accurately disclosed as omitted.

The first closed instance uses the genuine three-outcome omit-one design, with inclusion probabilities 2/3 and positive class totals (2/3,4/3). Integer compatibility forces class sizes (1,2). For the known-size instance, m=(500,500) with per-unit probabilities (1/10 on zeros, 1/5 on ones) realizes totals (50,100) and N=1000. More generally m=(1000-k,k), 500<=k<=750, is realized by uniformly choosing 50 zeros and 100 ones; the probabilities 50/(1000-k) and 100/k satisfy the bounds. Exact arithmetic confirms all 251 compatible means and all four continuous-box extrema. The omitted specified weight evaluations and known-size sampling construction are accurately disclosed.

Closed rational calculation on nonempty binary samples: 44 ones in 48 observations, 108 in 160, and 291 in 579. Independent Fraction arithmetic verified uniqueness of the three inferred counts, all 42 cell roundings, all six exact corrected values and differences, no rounding ties, and every stated grid comparison. All binary-formula denominators are positive for the displayed proportions and gamma values.

Take n=2, y=(0,1), (alpha,beta)=(1/4,1/2) and (alpha',beta')=(1/2,1); both ratios are 2. The first box contains (4,2) and (2,4), producing the distinct values 1/3 and 2/3, as compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean. Taking both bounds equal to 1/2 also realizes the ratio-one clause. In general n>0 and strictly positive box weights keep all denominators positive, and positive scaling maps the two boxes to the same normalized box.

Compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean: n=3, y=(0,0,1), alpha=1/4, beta=1/2, gamma=2, kL=kH=2. Both least-cut predicates hold, the observations 0 and 1 are genuinely tied, and both physical weight vectors give that pair equal weights. A constant vector also has valid cut 0. An independent finite enumeration checked 332 sorted sample/ratio instances including ties and gamma=1. The separate no-cut formulation and Supplement steps (i)-(iv) are accurately disclosed as omitted.

The mixed sample n=2,y=(0,1),alpha=1/4,beta=1/2 has endpoints 1/3 and 2/3, with explicit feasible weights compiled in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean. Singleton samples y=0 and y=1 realize the two degenerate p cases; equal positive bounds realize gamma=1. For every allowed sample p lies in [0,1], gamma>=1 and both displayed denominators are positive. Independent variation of the total weights on ones and zeros gives exactly the stated closed interval.

The compiled empty-or-census design in scratch/Nonvacuity.lean satisfies every hypothesis with N=J=2, y=(0,1), alpha=1/4, beta=3/4 and class map id. Its class totals are (1/2,1/2); at gamma=3 both threshold values at cut 0 are 1/2, and at cut 1 the lower/upper values are 1/4 and 3/4, so none equals its compared outcome. The joint law is a probability measure. Thus separation, positivity and the finite cut domain are jointly satisfiable without assuming convergence.
